entries.originalText: The Voice of the Disciple
entries.modernizedText: The Voice of the Disciple

entries.originalText: Trusting in Thy goodness and great mercy, O Lord, I draw near, the sick to the Healer, the hungering and thirsting to the Fountain of life, the poverty-stricken to the King of heaven, the servant to the Lord, the creature to the Creator, the desolate to my own gentle Comforter.
entries.modernizedText: Trusting in Your goodness and great mercy, O Lord, I draw near: the sick to the Healer, the hungry and thirsty to the Fountain of life, the poor to the King of heaven, the servant to the Lord, the creature to the Creator, the desolate to my own gentle Comforter.

entries.originalText: But whence is this unto me, that Thou comest unto me?
entries.modernizedText: But how is it granted to me that You come to me?

entries.originalText: Who am I that Thou shouldest offer me Thyself?
entries.modernizedText: Who am I that You should offer Yourself to me?

entries.originalText: How doth a sinner dare to appear before Thee?
entries.modernizedText: How does a sinner dare to appear before You?

entries.originalText: And how dost thou vouchsafe to come to the sinner?
entries.modernizedText: And how do You graciously come to the sinner?

entries.originalText: Thou knowest Thy servant, and Thou knowest that he hath in him no good thing for which Thou shouldest grant him this grace.
entries.modernizedText: You know Your servant, and You know that he has in him no good thing for which You should grant him this grace.

entries.originalText: I confess therefore mine own vileness, I acknowledge Thy goodness, I praise Thy tenderness, and I give Thee thanks for Thine exceeding great love.
entries.modernizedText: I confess therefore my own vileness, acknowledge Your goodness, praise Your tenderness, and give You thanks for Your exceedingly great love.

entries.originalText: For Thou doest this for Thine own sake, not for my merits, that Thy goodness may be more manifest unto me, Thy charity more abundantly poured out upon me, and Thy humility more perfectly commended unto me.
entries.modernizedText: For You do this for Your own sake, not for my merits, so that Your goodness may be more manifest to me, Your charity more abundantly poured out upon me, and Your humility more perfectly commended to me.

entries.originalText: Therefore because this pleaseth Thee and Thou hast commanded that thus it shall be, Thy condescension pleaseth me also; and oh that mine iniquity hinder it not.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, because this pleases You and You have commanded that it be so, Your condescension pleases me also; and oh, may my iniquity not hinder it.

entries.originalText: O most sweet and tender Jesus, what reverence, what giving of thanks is due to Thee with perpetual praise for the receiving of Thy sacred Body and Blood, the dignity whereof no man is found able to express.
entries.modernizedText: O most sweet and tender Jesus, what reverence, what thanksgiving with perpetual praise is due to You for receiving Your sacred Body and Blood, whose dignity no one is able to express.

entries.originalText: But what shall I think upon in this Communion in approaching my Lord, whom I am not able worthily to honour, and nevertheless whom I long devoutly to receive?
entries.modernizedText: But what shall I think upon in this Communion as I approach my Lord, whom I cannot worthily honor and yet long devoutly to receive?

entries.originalText: What shall be better and more healthful meditation for me, than utter humiliation of myself before Thee, and exaltation of Thine infinite goodness towards me?
entries.modernizedText: What better and more wholesome meditation could there be for me than utter humiliation of myself before You and exaltation of Your infinite goodness toward me?

entries.originalText: I praise Thee, O my God, and exalt Thee for evermore.
entries.modernizedText: I praise You, O my God, and exalt You forever.

entries.originalText: I despise myself, and cast myself down before Thee into the deep of my vileness.
entries.modernizedText: I despise myself and cast myself down before You into the depths of my vileness.

entries.originalText: Behold, Thou art the Saint of saints and I the refuse of sinners; behold, Thou stoopest unto me who am not worthy to look upon Thee; behold, Thou comest unto me, Thou willest to be with me, Thou invitest me to Thy feast.
entries.modernizedText: See, You are the Saint of saints and I the refuse of sinners; see, You stoop to me, who am not worthy to look upon You; see, You come to me, You will to be with me, You invite me to Your feast.

entries.originalText: Thou willest to give me the heavenly food and bread of angels to eat; none other, in truth, than Thyself, The living bread, which didst descend from heaven; and givest life to the world.(1)
entries.modernizedText: You will to give me heavenly food and the bread of angels to eat; none other, in truth, than Yourself, the living bread, who descended from heaven and gives life to the world.(1)

entries.originalText: Behold, whence this love proceedeth! what manner of condescension shineth forth herein.
entries.modernizedText: See from where this love proceeds! What condescension shines forth here!

entries.originalText: What great giving of thanks and praise is due unto Thee for these benefits!
entries.modernizedText: What great thanksgiving and praise are due to You for these benefits!

entries.originalText: Oh how salutary and profitable Thy purpose when Thou didst ordain this!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, how wholesome and profitable was Your purpose when You ordained this!

entries.originalText: How sweet and pleasant the feast when Thou didst give Thyself for food!
entries.modernizedText: How sweet and pleasant the feast when You gave Yourself for food!

entries.originalText: Oh how admirable is thy working, O Lord, how mighty Thy power, how unspeakable Thy truth!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, how admirable is Your work, O Lord, how mighty Your power, how unspeakable Your truth!

entries.originalText: For Thou didst speak the word, and all things were made; and this is done which Thou hast commanded.
entries.modernizedText: For You spoke the word, and all things were made; and what You have commanded is done.

entries.originalText: A thing wonderful, and worthy of faith, and surpassing all the understanding of man, that Thou, O Lord my God, very God and very man, givest Thyself altogether to us in a little bread and wine, and art so our inexhaustible food.
entries.modernizedText: It is wonderful, worthy of faith, and beyond all human understanding that You, O Lord my God, true God and true man, give Yourself altogether to us in a little bread and wine, and are thus our inexhaustible food.

entries.originalText: Thou, O Lord of all, who hast need of nothing, hast willed to dwell in us through Thy Sacrament.
entries.modernizedText: You, O Lord of all, who need nothing, have willed to dwell in us through Your Sacrament.

entries.originalText: Preserve my heart and my body undefiled, that with a joyful and pure conscience I may be able very often to [celebrate, and](2) receive to my perpetual health.
entries.modernizedText: Preserve my heart and my body undefiled, so that with a joyful and pure conscience I may very often [celebrate, and](2) receive to my lasting health

entries.originalText: Thy mysteries, which Thou hast consecrated and instituted both for Thine own honour, and for a perpetual memorial.
entries.modernizedText: Your mysteries, which You have consecrated and instituted both for Your own honor and for a perpetual memorial.

entries.originalText: Rejoice, O my soul, and give thanks unto God for so great a gift and precious consolation, left unto thee in this vale of tears.
entries.modernizedText: Rejoice, O my soul, and give thanks to God for so great a gift and precious consolation, left to you in this valley of tears.

entries.originalText: For so oft as thou callest this mystery to mind and receivest the body of Christ, so often dost thou celebrate the work of thy redemption, and art made partaker of all the merits of Christ.
entries.modernizedText: For as often as you call this mystery to mind and receive the body of Christ, you celebrate the work of your redemption and are made a partaker of all the merits of Christ.

entries.originalText: For the charity of Christ never groweth less, and the greatness of His propitiation is never exhausted.
entries.modernizedText: For the charity of Christ never grows less, and the greatness of His propitiation is never exhausted.

entries.originalText: Therefore, by continual renewal of thy spirit, thou oughtest to dispose thyself hereunto and to weigh the great mystery of salvation with attentive consideration.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, by continually renewing your spirit, you ought to prepare yourself for this and weigh the great mystery of salvation with attentive consideration.

entries.originalText: So great, new, and joyful ought it to appear to thee when thou comest to communion, as if on this self-same day Christ for the first time were descending into the Virgin’s womb and becoming man, or hanging on the cross, suffering and dying for the salvation of mankind.
entries.modernizedText: It ought to appear to you as great, new, and joyful when you come to communion as if on this very day Christ were for the first time descending into the Virgin’s womb and becoming man, or hanging on the cross, suffering and dying for the salvation of humankind.
